explanation_en: 'Mann' means 'man' in German. It takes the article 'der' (masculine).

question.en: The man is reading a book.

explanation_en: 'Mann' means 'man'. It is the subject of this sentence, so it uses the nominative form with 'der'.

question.de: Ich sehe den _____ auf der Straße.
question.en: I see the man on the street.

explanation_en: 'Mann' is the direct object here, so it takes the accusative case: 'den Mann' (masculine accusative).
'Frau' means 'woman' in German. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Note: 'Frau' also means 'Mrs.' as a title.

question.en: The woman comes from Austria.

explanation_en: 'Frau' means 'woman'. As the subject, it uses nominative 'die Frau'.

question.en: He knows the woman well.

explanation_en: 'Frau' is the direct object here. Feminine nouns keep 'die' in the accusative case: 'die Frau'.
'Kind' means 'child' in German. It takes the neuter article 'das'. The plural is 'Kinder' (children).

question.en: The child is very tired.

explanation_en: 'Kind' means 'child'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Kind' in the nominative.

question.en: The parents love their child.

explanation_en: 'Kind' (child) is the direct object. Neuter nouns keep 'das/ihr' in the accusative case: 'ihr Kind'.
'Tag' means 'day' in German. It takes the masculine article 'der'. The plural is 'Tage'.

question.en: The day starts early.

explanation_en: 'Tag' means 'day'. As the sentence subject, it uses nominative 'der Tag'.

question.de: Wir haben sieben _____ in einer Woche.
question.en: We have seven days in a week.

explanation_en: The plural of 'Tag' is 'Tage'. In the accusative (after 'haben'), it stays 'Tage'.
'Jahr' means 'year' in German. It is neuter: 'das Jahr'. Plural: 'Jahre'.

question.en: The year 2024 was very interesting.

explanation_en: 'Jahr' means 'year'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Jahr' in the nominative.

question.en: I have been learning German for a year.

explanation_en: After 'seit' (for/since), the dative case is used: 'seit einem Jahr'. 'Jahr' stays the same in dative singular.
'Zeit' means 'time' in German. It is feminine: 'die Zeit'. Plural: 'Zeiten'.

question.en: Time passes quickly.

explanation_en: 'Zeit' means 'time'. As a feminine noun in the nominative, it uses 'die Zeit'.

question.en: Do you have time for a conversation?

explanation_en: 'Zeit' is used without an article here (no time = keine Zeit, some time = Zeit). This is common with abstract nouns in German.
'Haus' means 'house' in German. It is neuter: 'das Haus'. Plural: 'Häuser' (note the umlaut).

question.en: The house has a garden.

explanation_en: 'Haus' means 'house'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Haus' as the sentence subject.

question.en: We are buying a new house.

explanation_en: 'Haus' is the accusative direct object here. Neuter nouns use 'ein Haus' in the accusative (same as nominative for neuter).
'Arbeit' means 'work' or 'job' in German. It is feminine: 'die Arbeit'. Plural: 'Arbeiten'.

question.en: The work is fun for me.

explanation_en: 'Arbeit' means 'work'. As the sentence subject, it uses the nominative 'die Arbeit'.

question.en: He is looking for a new job.

explanation_en: 'Arbeit' here means 'job'. After 'eine' (feminine indefinite accusative), 'Arbeit' is the direct object. Feminine accusative: 'eine Arbeit'.
'Schule' means 'school' in German. It is feminine: 'die Schule'. Plural: 'Schulen'.

question.en: The child goes to school.

explanation_en: 'in die Schule' means 'to school'. After 'in' with direction of movement, the accusative is used: 'die Schule' (feminine accusative).

question.de: Es gibt viele _____ in dieser Stadt.
question.en: There are many schools in this city.

explanation_en: The plural of 'Schule' is 'Schulen'. After 'viele' (many), use the plural form.
'Stadt' means 'city' or 'town' in German. It is feminine: 'die Stadt'. Plural: 'Städte' (with umlaut).

question.en: The city has many parks.

explanation_en: 'Stadt' means 'city'. As a feminine noun, it uses 'die Stadt' in the nominative.

question.de: Er fährt in die _____ zum Einkaufen.
question.en: He goes into the city to go shopping.

explanation_en: 'in die Stadt' uses accusative because there is movement toward the city (direction). Feminine accusative: 'die Stadt'.
'Land' means 'country' in German. It is neuter: 'das Land'. Plural: 'Länder' (with umlaut). It can also mean 'countryside'.

question.en: The country has many inhabitants.

explanation_en: 'Land' means 'country'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Land' in the nominative.

question.en: There are many countries in Europe.

explanation_en: The plural of 'Land' is 'Länder' (with umlaut). After 'viele' (many), use the plural form.
'Geld' means 'money' in German. It is neuter: 'das Geld'. It is usually used without a plural (uncountable).

question.en: The money is on the table.

explanation_en: 'Geld' means 'money'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Geld' in the nominative.

question.en: She gives him the money back.

explanation_en: 'Geld' is the accusative direct object here ('gives back what?'). Neuter accusative: 'das Geld' (same form as nominative).
'Auto' means 'car' in German. It is neuter: 'das Auto'. Plural: 'Autos'. Short for 'Automobil'.

question.en: The car is parked in front of the house.

explanation_en: 'Auto' means 'car'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Auto' in the nominative.

question.en: He is buying a new car.

explanation_en: 'Auto' is the accusative direct object. Neuter nouns take 'ein Auto' in the accusative (same as nominative for neuter).
'Tisch' means 'table' in German. It is masculine: 'der Tisch'. Plural: 'Tische'.

question.en: The table is made of wood.

explanation_en: 'Tisch' means 'table'. As a masculine noun, it uses 'der Tisch' in the nominative.

question.de: Sie stellen das Essen auf den _____ .
question.en: They put the food on the table.

explanation_en: 'auf den Tisch' uses the accusative because there is movement (putting something onto the table). Masculine accusative: 'den Tisch'.
'Tür' means 'door' in German. It is feminine: 'die Tür'. Plural: 'Türen'.

question.en: Please close the door.

explanation_en: 'Tür' means 'door'. 'die Tür' is the accusative direct object (close what? the door). Feminine accusative = same as nominative: 'die Tür'.

question.en: He knocks on the door.

explanation_en: 'an die Tür' uses the accusative because of directed movement (knocking toward/at the door). Feminine accusative: 'die Tür'.
'Straße' means 'street' in German. It is feminine: 'die Straße'. Plural: 'Straßen'. The ß (Eszett) represents a long 's' sound.

question.en: The child plays on the street.

explanation_en: 'auf der Straße' uses the dative (location, not movement). Feminine dative: 'der Straße'.

question.en: He lives in the next street.

explanation_en: 'in der nächsten Straße' uses the dative (location). Feminine dative: 'der Straße'.
'Familie' means 'family' in German. It is feminine: 'die Familie'. Plural: 'Familien'.

question.en: My family is very big.

explanation_en: 'Familie' means 'family'. With possessive 'meine' (my — feminine nominative), it remains 'meine Familie'.

question.en: He visits his family at the weekend.

explanation_en: 'Familie' is the accusative direct object. With 'seine' (his — feminine accusative), it stays 'seine Familie'.
'Freund' means 'friend' (male) in German. It is masculine: 'der Freund'. Plural: 'Freunde'. The female form is 'Freundin'. Note: 'Freund/Freundin' also means boyfriend/girlfriend in context.

question.en: He is my best friend.

explanation_en: 'Freund' means 'friend (male)'. As a masculine nominative, it uses 'mein Freund' or 'der Freund'.

question.en: I am visiting my friend in Hamburg.

explanation_en: 'Freund' is the accusative direct object. Masculine accusative: 'meinen Freund' (note the -en ending on the possessive).
'Wasser' means 'water' in German. It is neuter: 'das Wasser'. Plural: 'Wässer' (mostly used for mineral waters).

question.en: I drink a glass of water.

explanation_en: 'Wasser' means 'water'. After 'ein Glas' (a glass of), use the noun without article: 'ein Glas Wasser'.

question.en: Have you already ordered the water?

explanation_en: 'Wasser' is the accusative direct object. Neuter accusative: 'das Wasser' (same form as nominative).
'Buch' means 'book' in German. It is neuter: 'das Buch'. Plural: 'Bücher' (with umlaut).

question.en: The book is lying on the table.

explanation_en: 'Buch' means 'book'. As a neuter noun in the nominative, it uses 'das Buch'.

question.en: He is reading a book about history.

explanation_en: 'Buch' is the accusative direct object. Neuter indefinite accusative: 'ein Buch' (same as nominative for neuter).
'Frage' means 'question' in German. It is feminine: 'die Frage'. Plural: 'Fragen'.

question.en: The question is not simple.

explanation_en: 'Frage' means 'question'. As a feminine noun in the nominative, it uses 'die Frage'.

question.en: He answers all the questions.

explanation_en: The plural of 'Frage' is 'Fragen'. After 'alle' (all), use the plural form.
'Wort' means 'word' in German. It is neuter: 'das Wort'. It has two plurals: 'Wörter' (individual words) and 'Worte' (words in context or quotations).

question.en: The word is very long.

explanation_en: 'Wort' means 'word'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Wort' in the nominative.

question.de: Im Deutschen gibt es viele lange _____.
question.en: In German there are many long words.

explanation_en: Use 'Wörter' for individual separate words (e.g. in a list or dictionary). 'Worte' is used for words in a meaningful context ('seine letzten Worte' = his last words).
'Nummer' means 'number' in German. It is feminine: 'die Nummer'. Plural: 'Nummern'. Used for identifiers like phone numbers, house numbers.

question.en: What is your phone number?

explanation_en: 'Telefonnummer' is a compound noun (Telefon + Nummer). German frequently combines nouns into one long word. The gender is determined by the last noun: 'die Nummer' → 'die Telefonnummer'.

question.en: He wrote down the number.

explanation_en: 'Nummer' is the accusative direct object. Feminine accusative: 'die Nummer' (same form as nominative).
'Stuhl' means 'chair' in German. It is masculine: 'der Stuhl'. Plural: 'Stühle' (with umlaut).

question.en: Please take a chair.

explanation_en: 'Stuhl' means 'chair'. As a masculine accusative with indefinite article: 'einen Stuhl' (note the -en ending on 'ein').

question.en: She stands on the chair.

explanation_en: 'auf den Stuhl' uses the accusative because of upward directed movement. Masculine accusative: 'den Stuhl'.
'Essen' means 'food' or 'meal' in German. It is neuter: 'das Essen'. It comes from the verb 'essen' (to eat). The plural 'Essen' is the same as the singular.

question.en: The meal is ready.

explanation_en: 'Essen' means 'meal' or 'food'. As a neuter noun, it uses 'das Essen' in the nominative.

question.en: I am ordering the food for everyone.

explanation_en: 'Essen' is the accusative direct object. Neuter accusative: 'das Essen' (same form as nominative).
'Mutter' means 'mother'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.de: Die _____ liest dem Kind ein Buch vor.
question.en: The mother reads a book to the child.

explanation_en: 'Mutter' means 'mother'. It is the subject here, used in the nominative with 'die'.

question.de: Ich rufe meine _____ jeden Sonntag an.
question.en: I call my mother every Sunday.

explanation_en: After the possessive 'meine', 'Mutter' is used in the accusative case — but its form does not change (feminine accusative = same as nominative).
'Vater' means 'father'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.de: Der _____ spielt mit seinem Sohn im Garten.
question.en: The father plays with his son in the garden.

explanation_en: 'Vater' means 'father'. It is the subject of the sentence, used in the nominative with 'der'.

question.en: I visit my father at the weekend.

explanation_en: After 'meinen', 'Vater' is in the accusative case (masculine accusative adds -n to the article: 'meinen Vater').
'Bruder' means 'brother'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.de: Mein _____ ist zwei Jahre älter als ich.
question.en: My brother is two years older than me.

explanation_en: 'Bruder' means 'brother'. After 'mein' (nominative, masculine), the noun does not change.

question.de: Ich habe meinen _____ lange nicht gesehen.
question.en: I haven't seen my brother for a long time.

explanation_en: 'sehen' takes the accusative. 'meinen Bruder' — masculine accusative uses 'meinen' + the noun unchanged.
'Schwester' means 'sister'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.en: My sister studies in Berlin.

explanation_en: 'Schwester' means 'sister'. After 'meine' (nominative, feminine), the noun is unchanged.

question.en: I miss my sister very much.

explanation_en: 'vermissen' takes the accusative. Feminine nouns look the same in nominative and accusative: 'meine Schwester'.
'Eltern' means 'parents'. It is a plural-only noun and always uses 'die'.

question.en: My parents live in the countryside.

explanation_en: 'Eltern' means 'parents' and is always plural. 'Meine Eltern' uses the plural possessive form.

question.en: I visit my parents every Christmas.

explanation_en: 'Eltern' is plural-only. In the accusative, plural nouns take 'die' / 'meine' — the form is the same as nominative.
'Lehrer' means 'teacher' (male). It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: Our teacher always comes on time.

explanation_en: 'Lehrer' means 'teacher'. After 'unser' (nominative, masculine), the noun is unchanged.

question.en: The pupils like their teacher very much.

explanation_en: 'mögen' takes the accusative. 'ihren Lehrer' — masculine accusative uses 'ihren' before the noun.
'Arzt' means 'doctor'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The doctor examines the patient.

explanation_en: 'Arzt' means 'doctor'. It is the nominative subject here, used with 'der'.

question.en: I have to go to the doctor tomorrow.

explanation_en: After 'zum' (= zu + dem), the dative case is used. Masculine nouns do not change form in the dative: 'zum Arzt'.
'Kollege' means 'colleague'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: My colleague lives nearby.

explanation_en: 'Kollege' means 'colleague'. After 'mein' (nominative, masculine) the noun is unchanged.

question.de: Ich treffe meinen _____ nach der Arbeit.
question.en: I am meeting my colleague after work.

explanation_en: 'Kollege' is a weak masculine noun (N-Deklination). In the accusative, it adds -n: 'meinen Kollegen'.
'Nachbar' means 'neighbour'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: Our neighbour is very friendly.

explanation_en: 'Nachbar' means 'neighbour'. After 'unser' (nominative, masculine), the noun is unchanged.

question.de: Ich habe meinen _____ heute nicht gesehen.
question.en: I haven't seen my neighbour today.

explanation_en: 'Nachbar' is a weak masculine noun. In the accusative, it takes -n: 'meinen Nachbarn'.
'Chef' means 'boss' or 'head'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: My boss gives me a lot of work.

explanation_en: 'Chef' means 'boss'. After 'mein' (nominative, masculine), the noun is unchanged.

question.de: Ich muss meinen _____ um Erlaubnis fragen.
question.en: I have to ask my boss for permission.

explanation_en: After 'meinen' (masculine accusative), 'Chef' is unchanged — it is a regular (strong) masculine noun, not weak declension.
'Zimmer' means 'room'. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.en: The room has a large window.

explanation_en: 'Zimmer' means 'room'. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Ich suche ein _____ in der Stadtmitte.
question.en: I am looking for a room in the city centre.

explanation_en: After 'ein' (indefinite article, neuter accusative), 'Zimmer' is unchanged — neuter nouns have the same form in nominative and accusative.
'Küche' means 'kitchen'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.en: The kitchen has just been renovated.

explanation_en: 'Küche' means 'kitchen'. It is the feminine subject here, used with 'die'.

question.en: We have just painted the kitchen.

explanation_en: 'haben … gestrichen' uses the accusative for the object. Feminine nouns look the same in nominative and accusative: 'die Küche'.
'Garten' means 'garden'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The garden needs a lot of water.

explanation_en: 'Garten' means 'garden'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.en: We tend our garden every weekend.

explanation_en: 'pflegen' takes the accusative. 'unseren Garten' — masculine accusative uses 'unseren' + the noun.
'Bahnhof' means 'train station'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.de: Der _____ ist sehr groß und modern.
question.en: The train station is very large and modern.

explanation_en: 'Bahnhof' means 'train station'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: Ich fahre zum _____, um meinen Zug zu nehmen.
question.en: I go to the train station to catch my train.

explanation_en: 'zum' = zu + dem (dative). Masculine nouns in the dative with 'dem' are unchanged: 'zum Bahnhof'.
'Büro' means 'office'. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.en: The office opens at nine o'clock.

explanation_en: 'Büro' means 'office'. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Er verlässt sein _____ um sechs Uhr abends.
question.en: He leaves his office at six in the evening.

explanation_en: After 'sein' (possessive, neuter accusative), 'Büro' is unchanged — neuter nominative and accusative forms are identical.
'Fenster' means 'window'. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.en: The window lets in a lot of light.

explanation_en: 'Fenster' means 'window'. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Bitte schließ das _____, es ist kalt.
question.en: Please close the window, it is cold.

explanation_en: 'schließen' takes the accusative. Neuter nouns use 'das' in both nominative and accusative: 'das Fenster'.
'Bett' means 'bed'. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.en: The bed stands by the window.

explanation_en: 'Bett' means 'bed'. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Ich gehe um elf Uhr ins _____.
question.en: I go to bed at eleven o'clock.

explanation_en: 'ins' = in + das (accusative, showing movement into a place). 'ins Bett gehen' is a fixed phrase meaning 'to go to bed'.
'Handy' means 'mobile phone' in German. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.de: Das _____ ist neu und sehr teuer.
question.en: The mobile phone is new and very expensive.

explanation_en: 'Handy' means 'mobile phone' in German. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Ich habe mein _____ zu Hause vergessen.
question.en: I forgot my mobile phone at home.

explanation_en: After 'mein' (possessive, neuter accusative), 'Handy' is unchanged — neuter nominative and accusative are identical.
'Tasche' means 'bag' or 'pocket'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.en: The bag is on the chair.

explanation_en: 'Tasche' means 'bag'. It is the feminine subject, used with 'die'.

question.de: Ich packe meine _____ für die Reise.
question.en: I am packing my bag for the trip.

explanation_en: After 'meine' (possessive, feminine accusative), 'Tasche' is unchanged — feminine nominative and accusative are identical.
'Schlüssel' means 'key'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The key does not fit the lock.

explanation_en: 'Schlüssel' means 'key'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.en: I have lost my key.

explanation_en: 'verloren haben' takes the accusative. 'meinen Schlüssel' — masculine accusative uses 'meinen'. The noun itself is unchanged.
'Brief' means 'letter' (written correspondence). It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The letter is in the letterbox.

explanation_en: 'Brief' means 'letter'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.en: I am writing my grandmother a letter.

explanation_en: 'schreiben' here takes a dative object (meiner Oma) and an accusative object (einen Brief). 'Brief' is masculine accusative: 'einen Brief'.
'Stunde' means 'hour' (and also 'lesson' in school context). It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.en: The German lesson was very interesting.

explanation_en: 'Stunde' means both 'hour' and 'lesson'. It is the feminine subject here, used with 'die'.

question.de: Ich warte seit einer _____ auf den Bus.
question.en: I have been waiting for a bus for an hour.

explanation_en: 'seit einer Stunde' — 'seit' takes the dative. Feminine dative: 'einer Stunde' (the noun itself is unchanged).
'Woche' means 'week'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.de: Diese _____ lerne ich jeden Tag Deutsch.
question.en: This week I am learning German every day.

explanation_en: 'Woche' means 'week'. After 'diese' (demonstrative, feminine nominative), the noun is unchanged.

question.de: In einer _____ fahre ich nach München.
question.en: In one week I am travelling to Munich.

explanation_en: 'In einer Woche' — 'in' with dative for time expressions. Feminine dative: 'einer Woche' (the noun is unchanged).
'Monat' means 'month'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The month of May is my favourite month.

explanation_en: 'Monat' means 'month'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: In diesem _____ haben wir viel Regen.
question.en: This month we have a lot of rain.

explanation_en: 'In diesem Monat' — 'in' with dative for time. 'diesem' is the masculine dative demonstrative. The noun 'Monat' is unchanged.
'Morgen' (with capital M) means 'morning'. It is a masculine noun. Note: 'morgen' (lowercase) means 'tomorrow'.

question.en: The morning is my favourite time of day.

explanation_en: 'Morgen' means 'morning'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: Am _____ trinke ich immer eine Tasse Kaffee.
question.en: In the morning I always drink a cup of coffee.

explanation_en: 'Am Morgen' = 'in the morning'. 'am' = an + dem (dative). Masculine dative: 'dem Morgen' → 'am Morgen'.
'Abend' means 'evening'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The evening starts after work.

explanation_en: 'Abend' means 'evening'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.en: In the evening we often go for a walk.

explanation_en: 'Am Abend' = 'in the evening'. 'am' = an + dem (dative masculine). The noun itself is unchanged.
'Nacht' means 'night'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.de: Die _____ ist sehr dunkel und ruhig.
question.en: The night is very dark and quiet.

explanation_en: 'Nacht' means 'night'. It is the feminine subject, used with 'die'.

question.de: In der _____ kann ich nicht schlafen.
question.en: At night I cannot sleep.

explanation_en: 'In der Nacht' = 'at night'. 'in der' is feminine dative. The noun 'Nacht' is unchanged.
'Brot' means 'bread'. It is a neuter noun taking the article 'das'.

question.de: Das _____ kommt frisch aus der Bäckerei.
question.en: The bread comes fresh from the bakery.

explanation_en: 'Brot' means 'bread'. It is the neuter subject, used with 'das'.

question.de: Ich kaufe jeden Morgen ein frisches _____.
question.en: I buy a fresh loaf of bread every morning.

explanation_en: After 'ein frisches' (neuter accusative adjective), 'Brot' is unchanged — neuter nominative and accusative forms are identical.
'Milch' means 'milk'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'. It has no common plural form.

question.en: The milk in the fridge is cold.

explanation_en: 'Milch' means 'milk'. It is the feminine subject, used with 'die'.

question.en: Can you please buy the milk?

explanation_en: 'kaufen' takes the accusative. Feminine nouns look the same in nominative and accusative: 'die Milch'.
'Kaffee' means 'coffee'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The coffee smells wonderful.

explanation_en: 'Kaffee' means 'coffee'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: Ich trinke jeden Morgen meinen _____ ohne Zucker.
question.en: I drink my coffee without sugar every morning.

explanation_en: 'meinen Kaffee' — masculine accusative uses 'meinen'. The noun 'Kaffee' is unchanged.
'Sonne' means 'sun'. It is a feminine noun taking the article 'die'.

question.en: The sun rises in the east.

explanation_en: 'Sonne' means 'sun'. It is the feminine subject, used with 'die'.

question.de: Wir genießen die warme _____ am Strand.
question.en: We enjoy the warm sun on the beach.

explanation_en: 'genießen' takes the accusative. Feminine nouns look the same in nominative and accusative: 'die warme Sonne'.
'Regen' means 'rain'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The rain is very heavy today.

explanation_en: 'Regen' means 'rain'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: Wegen des starken _____ bleiben wir zu Hause.
question.en: Because of the heavy rain we are staying at home.

explanation_en: 'Wegen' takes the genitive case. Masculine genitive: 'des Regens' (adding -s to the noun).
'Berg' means 'mountain'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.de: Der _____ ist im Winter mit Schnee bedeckt.
question.en: The mountain is covered with snow in winter.

explanation_en: 'Berg' means 'mountain'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.de: Wir wandern auf den _____ und genießen die Aussicht.
question.en: We hike up the mountain and enjoy the view.

explanation_en: 'auf den Berg' — movement upward uses 'auf' + accusative. Masculine accusative: 'auf den Berg'.
'Fluss' means 'river'. It is a masculine noun taking the article 'der'.

question.en: The river flows through the city.

explanation_en: 'Fluss' means 'river'. It is the masculine subject, used with 'der'.

question.en: The doctor wears a white coat.

explanation_en: 'Kittel' (der Kittel, plural: die Kittel) means 'smock / (lab) coat'.

question.de: Im Labor muss jeder einen _____ anziehen.
question.en: In the lab everyone has to put on a lab coat.

explanation_en: 'Kittel' (der Kittel, plural: die Kittel) means 'smock / (lab) coat'.
'Sackgasse' means 'dead end / cul-de-sac'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Literal (street with no exit) and figurative (situation with no way forward).

question.de: Wir können hier nicht weiterfahren — das ist eine _____.
question.en: We can't drive on here — it's a dead end.

explanation_en: 'Sackgasse' (die Sackgasse, plural: die Sackgassen) means 'dead end / cul-de-sac'.

question.de: Die Verhandlungen sind in einer _____ gelandet.
question.en: The negotiations have ended up in a dead end.

explanation_en: 'Sackgasse' (die Sackgasse, plural: die Sackgassen) means 'dead end / cul-de-sac'.
'Empfehlung' means 'recommendation'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From empfehlen (to recommend). Common pattern: auf Empfehlung von = on the recommendation of.

question.de: Auf _____ meines Arztes mache ich jetzt mehr Sport.
question.en: On my doctor's recommendation I now do more sport.

explanation_en: 'Empfehlung' (die Empfehlung, plural: die Empfehlungen) means 'recommendation'.

question.de: Hast du eine _____ für ein gutes Restaurant?
question.en: Do you have a recommendation for a good restaurant?

explanation_en: 'Empfehlung' (die Empfehlung, plural: die Empfehlungen) means 'recommendation'.
'Verständnis' means 'understanding / sympathy'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). Key phrase: Verständnis haben für + Akk = to have sympathy/understanding for.

question.de: Ich habe volles _____ für deine Entscheidung.
question.en: I have full understanding for your decision.

explanation_en: 'Verständnis' (das Verständnis, plural: die Verständnisse) means 'understanding / sympathy'.

question.en: Thank you very much for your understanding.

explanation_en: 'Verständnis' (das Verständnis, plural: die Verständnisse) means 'understanding / sympathy'.
'Belästigung' means 'harassment / nuisance'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From belästigen (to harass/bother). Legal term: sexuelle Belästigung.

question.de: Sie meldete die _____ sofort der Polizei.
question.en: She reported the harassment to the police immediately.

explanation_en: 'Belästigung' (die Belästigung, plural: die Belästigungen) means 'harassment / nuisance'.

question.en: Constant advertising calls are a nuisance.

explanation_en: 'Belästigung' (die Belästigung, plural: die Belästigungen) means 'harassment / nuisance'.
'Auflage' means 'edition / print run; condition (imposed)'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Two senses: print run/edition of a publication, and an official condition attached to a permit.

question.de: Die erste _____ des Buches war schnell ausverkauft.
question.en: The first print run of the book sold out quickly.

explanation_en: 'Auflage' (die Auflage, plural: die Auflagen) means 'edition / print run; condition (imposed)'.

question.de: Die Behörde erteilte die Genehmigung nur unter strengen _____.
question.en: The authority granted the permit only under strict conditions.

explanation_en: 'Auflage' (die Auflage, plural: die Auflagen) means 'edition / print run; condition (imposed)'.

correct_answer: the specialist field / area of expertise
explanation_en: 'Fachgebiet' means 'specialist field / area of expertise'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). das Fach (subject) + das Gebiet (area). Related: der Fachmann, die Fachsprache.

question.en: Her specialist field is paediatrics.

explanation_en: 'Fachgebiet' (das Fachgebiet, plural: die Fachgebiete) means 'specialist field / area of expertise'.

question.de: Auf diesem _____ kennt er sich sehr gut aus.
question.en: He knows this field very well.

explanation_en: 'Fachgebiet' (das Fachgebiet, plural: die Fachgebiete) means 'specialist field / area of expertise'.
'Verwaltung' means 'administration'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From verwalten (to administer). Die öffentliche Verwaltung = public administration.

question.de: Die _____ der Stadt sucht neue Mitarbeiter.
question.en: The city administration is looking for new employees.

explanation_en: 'Verwaltung' (die Verwaltung, plural: die Verwaltungen) means 'administration'.

question.de: Er arbeitet seit Jahren in der _____.
question.en: He has worked in administration for years.

explanation_en: 'Verwaltung' (die Verwaltung, plural: die Verwaltungen) means 'administration'.
'Bruchteil' means 'fraction (of something)'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). der Bruch (break/fraction) + der Teil (part). Fixed phrase: im Bruchteil einer Sekunde.

question.de: Das kostet nur einen _____ des ursprünglichen Preises.
question.en: That costs only a fraction of the original price.

explanation_en: 'Bruchteil' (der Bruchteil, plural: die Bruchteile) means 'fraction (of something)'.

question.de: In einem _____ einer Sekunde war alles vorbei.
question.en: In a split second it was all over.

explanation_en: 'Bruchteil' (der Bruchteil, plural: die Bruchteile) means 'fraction (of something)'.
'Zwang' means 'compulsion / constraint / pressure'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). From zwingen (to force). Plural Zwänge = constraints. ohne Zwang = without pressure.

question.de: Niemand übt _____ auf dich aus — du entscheidest frei.
question.en: Nobody is putting pressure on you — you decide freely.

explanation_en: 'Zwang' (der Zwang, plural: die Zwänge) means 'compulsion / constraint / pressure'.

question.en: He suffers under social constraints.

explanation_en: 'Zwang' (der Zwang, plural: die Zwänge) means 'compulsion / constraint / pressure'.
'Ader' means 'vein / blood vessel'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Also figurative: eine musikalische Ader = a musical streak/talent.

question.en: The nurse finds the vein immediately.

explanation_en: 'Ader' (die Ader, plural: die Adern) means 'vein / blood vessel'.

question.de: Man sieht die blauen _____ an seinen Händen.
question.en: You can see the blue veins on his hands.

explanation_en: 'Ader' (die Ader, plural: die Adern) means 'vein / blood vessel'.
'Wohlbefinden' means 'well-being'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). wohl (well) + das Befinden (state of health). No plural. Compare: der Wohlstand (prosperity).

question.de: Regelmäßiger Schlaf ist wichtig für das _____.
question.en: Regular sleep is important for well-being.

explanation_en: 'Wohlbefinden' (das Wohlbefinden, no plural) means 'well-being'.

question.en: Yoga increases my physical well-being.

explanation_en: 'Wohlbefinden' (das Wohlbefinden, no plural) means 'well-being'.
'Suchtmittel' means 'addictive substance'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). die Sucht (addiction) + das Mittel (substance/means). Note the -mittel compound family.

question.de: Alkohol ist das am weitesten verbreitete _____.
question.en: Alcohol is the most widespread addictive substance.

explanation_en: 'Suchtmittel' (das Suchtmittel, plural: die Suchtmittel) means 'addictive substance'.

question.de: Der Verkauf von _____ an Jugendliche ist verboten.
question.en: Selling addictive substances to minors is prohibited.

explanation_en: 'Suchtmittel' (das Suchtmittel, plural: die Suchtmittel) means 'addictive substance'.
'Tatsache' means 'fact'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Key phrase: die Tatsache, dass … = the fact that … Related adverb: tatsächlich (actually).

question.de: Es ist eine _____, dass die Erde sich um die Sonne dreht.
question.en: It is a fact that the Earth revolves around the sun.

explanation_en: 'Tatsache' (die Tatsache, plural: die Tatsachen) means 'fact'.

question.en: We have to accept the facts.

explanation_en: 'Tatsache' (die Tatsache, plural: die Tatsachen) means 'fact'.
'Bedürfnis' means 'need'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). Pattern: ein Bedürfnis nach + Dativ = a need for. Related: bedürfen (to require).

question.de: Jeder Mensch hat das _____ nach Sicherheit.
question.en: Every person has the need for security.

explanation_en: 'Bedürfnis' (das Bedürfnis, plural: die Bedürfnisse) means 'need'.

question.en: Children have different needs than adults.

explanation_en: 'Bedürfnis' (das Bedürfnis, plural: die Bedürfnisse) means 'need'.
'Gräuel' means 'horror / atrocity'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). Related: grauenhaft (horrific), das Grauen (horror/dread). Mostly used in the plural for atrocities.

question.de: Der Bericht beschreibt die _____ des Krieges.
question.en: The report describes the atrocities of the war.

explanation_en: 'Gräuel' (der Gräuel, plural: die Gräuel) means 'horror / atrocity'.

question.de: Solche Taten sind ein _____ für jeden zivilisierten Menschen.
question.en: Such deeds are an abomination to every civilised person.

explanation_en: 'Gräuel' (der Gräuel, plural: die Gräuel) means 'horror / atrocity'.
'Empörung' means 'outrage / indignation'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From sich empören (to be outraged). Typical news collocation: Empörung auslösen.

question.en: The decision triggered great outrage.

explanation_en: 'Empörung' (die Empörung, no plural) means 'outrage / indignation'.

question.en: Full of indignation, she left the hall.

explanation_en: 'Empörung' (die Empörung, no plural) means 'outrage / indignation'.
'Entsetzen' means 'horror / dismay'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). Stronger than Schock in written German. Pattern: zu meinem Entsetzen = to my horror. Related adjective: entsetzlich.

question.de: Mit _____ sahen die Nachbarn das brennende Haus.
question.en: The neighbours watched the burning house with horror.

explanation_en: 'Entsetzen' (das Entsetzen, no plural) means 'horror / dismay'.

question.de: Zu meinem _____ war der Zug schon weg.
question.en: To my dismay, the train had already left.

explanation_en: 'Entsetzen' (das Entsetzen, no plural) means 'horror / dismay'.
'Geschwister' means 'siblings'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Plural-only noun: die Geschwister covers brothers and sisters together.

question.en: Do you have siblings?

explanation_en: 'Geschwister' (die Geschwister, plural: die Geschwister) means 'siblings'.

question.en: My siblings all live in Berlin.

explanation_en: 'Geschwister' (die Geschwister, plural: die Geschwister) means 'siblings'.
'Vorurteil' means 'prejudice'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). vor (before) + das Urteil (judgment) — literally judging before knowing. Pattern: Vorurteile gegenüber + Dativ.

question.de: Er hat viele _____ gegenüber anderen Kulturen.
question.en: He has many prejudices towards other cultures.

explanation_en: 'Vorurteil' (das Vorurteil, plural: die Vorurteile) means 'prejudice'.

question.de: Dieses _____ ist weit verbreitet, aber falsch.
question.en: This prejudice is widespread but wrong.

explanation_en: 'Vorurteil' (das Vorurteil, plural: die Vorurteile) means 'prejudice'.
'Nachfrage' means 'demand; inquiry'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Economics: Angebot und Nachfrage = supply and demand. Idiom: Danke der Nachfrage = thanks for asking.

question.de: Die _____ nach E-Bikes steigt jedes Jahr.
question.en: The demand for e-bikes rises every year.

explanation_en: 'Nachfrage' (die Nachfrage, plural: die Nachfragen) means 'demand; inquiry'.

question.de: Danke der _____ — mir geht es gut!
question.en: Thanks for asking — I'm fine!

explanation_en: 'Nachfrage' (die Nachfrage, plural: die Nachfragen) means 'demand; inquiry'.
'Benutzbarkeit' means 'usability'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). benutzbar (usable) + -keit. The -barkeit suffix turns 'can be X-ed' into a noun: Vorhersehbarkeit, Haltbarkeit.

question.de: Die _____ der App wurde stark verbessert.
question.en: The usability of the app has been greatly improved.

explanation_en: 'Benutzbarkeit' (die Benutzbarkeit, no plural) means 'usability'.

question.de: Bei Software zählt vor allem die _____.
question.en: With software, usability matters most.

explanation_en: 'Benutzbarkeit' (die Benutzbarkeit, no plural) means 'usability'.
'Vorhersehbarkeit' means 'predictability'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From vorhersehbar (foreseeable) ← vorhersehen (to foresee). Same family as die Vorhersage (forecast).

question.de: Die _____ seiner Reaktionen macht ihn leicht zu durchschauen.
question.en: The predictability of his reactions makes him easy to read.

explanation_en: 'Vorhersehbarkeit' (die Vorhersehbarkeit, no plural) means 'predictability'.

question.en: Children need routine and predictability.

explanation_en: 'Vorhersehbarkeit' (die Vorhersehbarkeit, no plural) means 'predictability'.
'Auswirkung' means 'effect / impact'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Pattern: Auswirkungen auf + Akk = effects on. Usually plural. Compare: die Wirkung (effect), die Ursache (cause).

question.de: Die _____ des Klimawandels sind schon heute spürbar.
question.en: The effects of climate change can already be felt today.

explanation_en: 'Auswirkung' (die Auswirkung, plural: die Auswirkungen) means 'effect / impact'.

question.de: Diese Entscheidung hat _____ auf uns alle.

explanation_en: 'Auswirkung' (die Auswirkung, plural: die Auswirkungen) means 'effect / impact'.
'Vielfalt' means 'diversity / variety'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). viel (much) + -falt (fold). Pattern: eine Vielfalt an + Dativ = a variety of.

question.de: Die kulturelle _____ macht diese Stadt besonders.
question.en: Cultural diversity makes this city special.

explanation_en: 'Vielfalt' (die Vielfalt, no plural) means 'diversity / variety'.

question.de: Der Markt bietet eine große _____ an frischem Gemüse.
question.en: The market offers a great variety of fresh vegetables.

explanation_en: 'Vielfalt' (die Vielfalt, no plural) means 'diversity / variety'.

'Sehnsucht' means 'longing / yearning'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Pattern: Sehnsucht nach + Dativ = longing for. One of the classic 'untranslatable' German words. Note the -sucht family: Eifersucht, Suchtmittel.

question.de: Sie hat große _____ nach ihrer Heimat.
question.en: She has a great longing for her home country.

explanation_en: 'Sehnsucht' (die Sehnsucht, plural: die Sehnsüchte) means 'longing / yearning'.

question.de: Voller _____ wartete er auf ihren Brief.
question.en: Full of longing, he waited for her letter.

explanation_en: 'Sehnsucht' (die Sehnsucht, plural: die Sehnsüchte) means 'longing / yearning'.

explanation_en: 'Gemeinde' (die Gemeinde, plural: die Gemeinden) means 'municipality / community / congregation'.

question.de: Die _____ trifft sich sonntags in der Kirche.
question.en: The congregation meets in the church on Sundays.

explanation_en: 'Gemeinde' (die Gemeinde, plural: die Gemeinden) means 'municipality / community / congregation'.
'Bilanz' means 'balance (sheet) / outcome / tally'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Business term and figurative: Bilanz ziehen = to take stock / sum up. News: die traurige Bilanz des Unfalls.

explanation_en: 'Bilanz' (die Bilanz, plural: die Bilanzen) means 'balance (sheet) / outcome / tally'.

explanation_en: 'Bilanz' (die Bilanz, plural: die Bilanzen) means 'balance (sheet) / outcome / tally'.

'Teilhabe' means 'participation / inclusion (in society)'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Political/social term: gesellschaftliche Teilhabe. Compare: die Teilnahme (taking part in an event), die Anteilnahme (sympathy).

question.de: Das Gesetz soll die _____ von Menschen mit Behinderung verbessern.
question.en: The law is meant to improve the participation of people with disabilities.

explanation_en: 'Teilhabe' (die Teilhabe, no plural) means 'participation / inclusion (in society)'.

question.de: Es ist meine _____, dir die Wahrheit zu sagen.

explanation_en: 'Pflicht' (die Pflicht, plural: die Pflichten) means 'duty / obligation'.

'Geflüchtete' means 'refugee (adjectival noun)'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). Adjectival noun from geflüchtet: der/die Geflüchtete, plural die Geflüchteten, ein Geflüchteter. Increasingly preferred over der Flüchtling in current usage.

question.en: Many refugees learn German very quickly.

explanation_en: 'Geflüchtete' (der Geflüchtete, plural: die Geflüchteten) means 'refugee (adjectival noun)'.

question.de: Die Stadt stellt Wohnungen für _____ bereit.
question.en: The city provides apartments for refugees.

explanation_en: 'Geflüchtete' (der Geflüchtete, plural: die Geflüchteten) means 'refugee (adjectival noun)'.

'Umweltschützer' means 'environmentalist'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). die Umwelt + der Schützer (protector, from schützen). Female form: die Umweltschützerin.

question.en: The environmentalists protest against the new power plant.

explanation_en: 'Umweltschützer' (der Umweltschützer, plural: die Umweltschützer) means 'environmentalist'.

question.de: Als _____ fährt er nur mit dem Fahrrad.
question.en: As an environmentalist he only travels by bike.

explanation_en: 'Umweltschützer' (der Umweltschützer, plural: die Umweltschützer) means 'environmentalist'.
'Erfassung' means 'recording / registration (of data)'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From erfassen (to capture/record). Bureaucratic staple: Datenerfassung, Zeiterfassung.

explanation_en: 'Erfassung' (die Erfassung, plural: die Erfassungen) means 'recording / registration (of data)'.

question.en: We use a form for registering new members.

explanation_en: 'Erfassung' (die Erfassung, plural: die Erfassungen) means 'recording / registration (of data)'.

question.en: According to a recent survey, young people read fewer books.

explanation_en: 'Erhebung' (die Erhebung, plural: die Erhebungen) means 'survey / collection (of data); elevation'.

explanation_en: 'Erhebung' (die Erhebung, plural: die Erhebungen) means 'survey / collection (of data); elevation'.

explanation_en: 'Regal' (das Regal, plural: die Regale) means 'shelf / shelving unit'.

question.de: Wir brauchen ein neues _____ für die Küche.
question.en: We need a new shelf for the kitchen.

explanation_en: 'Regal' (das Regal, plural: die Regale) means 'shelf / shelving unit'.
'Säure' means 'acid'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From sauer (sour/acidic). Chemistry and cooking: Magensäure, Zitronensäure.

question.en: Lemons contain a lot of acid.

explanation_en: 'Säure' (die Säure, plural: die Säuren) means 'acid'.

explanation_en: 'Farbdruck' (der Farbdruck, plural: die Farbdrucke) means 'colour print / colour printing'.

question.en: The owner of the car parked illegally.

explanation_en: 'Besitzer' (der Besitzer, plural: die Besitzer) means 'owner'.

question.en: The café has a new owner.

explanation_en: 'Besitzer' (der Besitzer, plural: die Besitzer) means 'owner'.
'Rechtsstreit' means 'legal dispute / lawsuit'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). das Recht + der Streit. Related: der Rechtsanwalt (lawyer), das Gericht (court), klagen (to sue).

explanation_en: 'Rechtsstreit' (der Rechtsstreit, plural: die Rechtsstreite) means 'legal dispute / lawsuit'.

question.de: Sie gewann den _____ um das Grundstück.

explanation_en: 'Rechtsstreit' (der Rechtsstreit, plural: die Rechtsstreite) means 'legal dispute / lawsuit'.

question.de: Das war keine _____ — es tut mir leid!
question.en: That wasn't intentional — I'm sorry!

explanation_en: 'Absicht' (die Absicht, plural: die Absichten) means 'intention'.

question.de: Er hat die _____, im Ausland zu studieren.
question.en: He intends to study abroad.

explanation_en: 'Absicht' (die Absicht, plural: die Absichten) means 'intention'.
'Hürde' means 'hurdle / obstacle'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). Sports and figurative: bürokratische Hürden. Near-synonym of das Hindernis, but Hürde implies something you can clear.

question.de: Die Sprache ist die größte _____ für viele Einwanderer.
question.en: The language is the biggest hurdle for many immigrants.

explanation_en: 'Hürde' (die Hürde, plural: die Hürden) means 'hurdle / obstacle'.

question.de: Der Läufer sprang elegant über jede _____.
question.en: The runner jumped elegantly over every hurdle.

explanation_en: 'Hürde' (die Hürde, plural: die Hürden) means 'hurdle / obstacle'.
'Hindernis' means 'obstacle'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). From hindern (to hinder). Compare die Hürde: a Hürde can be cleared, a Hindernis blocks the way.

question.de: Ein umgestürzter Baum war das erste _____ auf dem Weg.
question.en: A fallen tree was the first obstacle on the path.

explanation_en: 'Hindernis' (das Hindernis, plural: die Hindernisse) means 'obstacle'.

question.de: Fehlendes Geld ist kein _____ für gute Ideen.
question.en: A lack of money is no obstacle to good ideas.

explanation_en: 'Hindernis' (das Hindernis, plural: die Hindernisse) means 'obstacle'.
'Schrittgeschwindigkeit' means 'walking pace / walking speed'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). der Schritt (step) + die Geschwindigkeit (speed). Traffic sign vocabulary: ca. 4–7 km/h.

question.en: In the play street, walking pace applies.

explanation_en: 'Schrittgeschwindigkeit' (die Schrittgeschwindigkeit, no plural) means 'walking pace / walking speed'.

question.de: Die Autos kriechen im Stau mit _____ voran.
question.en: The cars creep forward at walking pace in the traffic jam.

explanation_en: 'Schrittgeschwindigkeit' (die Schrittgeschwindigkeit, no plural) means 'walking pace / walking speed'.

'Wahnsinn' means 'madness / insanity; (colloquial) awesome'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). Literal madness, but extremely common as an exclamation: Wahnsinn! = Wow! Adjective: wahnsinnig (insanely — wahnsinnig gut).

question.de: Es wäre _____, bei diesem Sturm zu segeln.
question.en: It would be madness to sail in this storm.

explanation_en: 'Wahnsinn' (der Wahnsinn, no plural) means 'madness / insanity; (colloquial) awesome'.

question.en: You finished the marathon? Awesome!

explanation_en: 'Wahnsinn' (der Wahnsinn, no plural) means 'madness / insanity; (colloquial) awesome'.
'Unzufriedenheit' means 'dissatisfaction'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). un- + zufrieden + -heit. Pattern: Unzufriedenheit mit + Dativ = dissatisfaction with.

question.de: Die _____ der Mitarbeiter wächst seit Monaten.
question.en: The employees' dissatisfaction has been growing for months.

explanation_en: 'Unzufriedenheit' (die Unzufriedenheit, no plural) means 'dissatisfaction'.

question.de: Aus _____ mit dem Service wechselte sie die Bank.
question.en: Out of dissatisfaction with the service, she changed banks.

explanation_en: 'Unzufriedenheit' (die Unzufriedenheit, no plural) means 'dissatisfaction'.

'Mittelstreifen' means 'median strip / central reservation'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). die Mitte + der Streifen (strip). Traffic family: der Seitenstreifen (hard shoulder), der Zebrastreifen (crosswalk).

question.de: Das Auto blieb auf dem _____ der Autobahn stehen.
question.en: The car came to a stop on the median strip of the motorway.

explanation_en: 'Mittelstreifen' (der Mittelstreifen, plural: die Mittelstreifen) means 'median strip / central reservation'.

question.de: Auf dem _____ wachsen Büsche und Gras.
question.en: Bushes and grass grow on the central reservation.

explanation_en: 'Mittelstreifen' (der Mittelstreifen, plural: die Mittelstreifen) means 'median strip / central reservation'.

'Betreuer' means 'carer / supervisor / counsellor'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). From betreuen (to look after). Contexts: Kinderbetreuer, Doktorvater/Betreuer (thesis supervisor), rechtlicher Betreuer (legal guardian).

question.de: Der _____ hilft den Kindern bei den Hausaufgaben.
question.en: The supervisor helps the children with their homework.

explanation_en: 'Betreuer' (der Betreuer, plural: die Betreuer) means 'carer / supervisor / counsellor'.

question.en: Every student gets a personal advisor.

explanation_en: 'Betreuer' (der Betreuer, plural: die Betreuer) means 'carer / supervisor / counsellor'.

'Stimmung' means 'mood / atmosphere'. It takes the article 'die' (feminine). From die Stimme (voice). gute/schlechte Stimmung; Stimmung machen = to get the crowd going. Compare: die Laune (personal mood).

question.de: Heute bin ich nicht in _____ zum Feiern.
question.en: Today I'm not in the mood for celebrating.

explanation_en: 'Stimmung' (die Stimmung, plural: die Stimmungen) means 'mood / atmosphere'.

question.de: Auf der Party herrschte eine tolle _____.
question.en: There was a great atmosphere at the party.

explanation_en: 'Stimmung' (die Stimmung, plural: die Stimmungen) means 'mood / atmosphere'.

'Erlebnis' means 'experience (single event)'. It takes the article 'das' (neuter). KEY CONTRAST: das Erlebnis = one memorable event you lived through; die Erfahrung = knowledge accumulated over time. Ein Bungee-Sprung ist ein Erlebnis; zehn Jahre Berufserfahrung ist Erfahrung.

question.en: The balloon ride was an unforgettable experience.

explanation_en: 'Erlebnis' (das Erlebnis, plural: die Erlebnisse) means 'experience (single event)'.

question.de: Erzähl mir von deinen _____ in Japan!
question.en: Tell me about your experiences in Japan!

explanation_en: 'Erlebnis' (das Erlebnis, plural: die Erlebnisse) means 'experience (single event)'.
'Ratschlag' means 'piece of advice'. It takes the article 'der' (masculine). der Rat + der Schlag. Ratschläge geben/befolgen. Compare: der Vorschlag (suggestion), der Hinweis (hint).

question.en: May I give you a piece of advice?

explanation_en: 'Ratschlag' (der Ratschlag, plural: die Ratschläge) means 'piece of advice'.

question.de: Ich habe seine _____ leider nicht befolgt.
question.en: Unfortunately, I didn't follow his advice.

explanation_en: 'Ratschlag' (der Ratschlag, plural: die Ratschläge) means 'piece of advice'.
